questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Dataset representativeness” in this lesson?
options: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
questions.answer_key: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.
questions.explanation: Dataset representativeness: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Bias and subgroup performance”, what should a learner verify?
options: Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.
questions.answer_key: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Privacy considerations”?
options: Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
questions.answer_key: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
